newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian government says takes last opposition town.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian government says takes last opposition town.

text.p: Cambodian government forces seized on Tuesday the last town held by loyalists of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, government military officials said.
The town of O'Smach fell at 1.10 p.m. (0610 GMT) and royalist troops were fleeing the area, said Nuo Sam, first deputy governor of the northwest province of Siem Reap.
A senior military official told Reuters the government forces, under the control of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, had captured O'Smach around 2 p.m. (0700 GMT) after a major offensive on Tuesday.
He said Hun Sen's troops had seized seven royalist tanks but had no information on any prisoners or casualties.
There was no confirmation available from the immediate area of the fighting, and a Thai military official on the border said he believed O'Smach remained in royalist hands.
O'Smach, a town near the Thai border, was the last major stronghold of Ranariddh's ragged army, which has been battling government forces since Hun Sen overthrew the prince on July 6.
Gun and mortar fire rocked O'Smach in the morning, officials on the border said earlier.
Hours earlier, more than 20,000 civilians fled O'Smach into Thailand to escape the fighting.

Thai authorities said they opened gates at a checkpoint and allowed the civilians to walk across the border to Kab Choeng district late on Monday after government troops captured the strategic hill of Khao Laem five km (three miles) from O'Smach.
The refugees spent the morning at a border market two km (one mile) inside Thailand and later moved on foot to Huay Choeng, six km (four miles) from the border.
The lines of fleeing Cambodians stretched the six km from the market to Huay Choeng, witnesses said.
The Thai army had sent reinforcements into the area and sealed the border in anticipation of Tuesday's fighting.
About 2,000 civilians remain in O'Smach, where Ranariddh's forces had dug in against Hun Sen's troops with assistance from the Khmer Rouge.

Major Yen Bunsrun of Ranariddh's army said earlier he was getting support from about 1,000 Khmer Rouge, Maoists who ruled Cambodia during the 1975-79 "Killing Fields" years, during which more than one million Cambodians died.
"Even if they capture the town, Hun Sen's troops will not be able to hold it for more than three days," he said.
Hun Sen has justified his power grab by accusing Ranariddh of smuggling weapons and bringing Khmer Rouge rebels into Phnom Penh. The prince has denied any wrongdoing.
